Beneath the Same Blue-Istanbul Modern.name: Beneath the Same Blue
Beneath the Same Blue-Istanbul Modern.description: Istanbul Modern’s 10th collection exhibition brings together works by artists from Türkiye and different parts of the world, produced across various periods and geographies, along historical and thematic axes. Spanning the museum’s Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Permanent Exhibition Gallery and different floors of the museum, the exhibition traces the transformation of modern and contemporary art in Türkiye since the 1940s, while offering new ways of reading the collection through encounters and…

Semiha Berksoy: Aria of All Colors-Istan.name: Semiha Berksoy: Aria of All Colors
Semiha Berksoy: Aria of All Colors-Istan.description: “Aria of All Colors,” a major exhibition devoted to Semiha Berksoy (1910–2004), celebrates a pioneering artist whose versatility and resolve enabled her to break new ground in both Türkiye and Europe. The exhibition brings together her expansive body of work – spanning the performing arts, visual arts, cinema, and literature – and offers a comprehensive look at the creative universe she built over the course of her extraordinary career. With more than 200 works on view, the exhibition makes…

Panorama: Dreams and Places-Istanbul Mod.name: Panorama: Dreams and Places
Panorama: Dreams and Places-Istanbul Mod.description: Aiming to present a thematic narrative on contemporary photography and lens-based art in Türkiye, “Panorama: Dreams and Places” brings together a comprehensive selection of works produced since the 2010s by 18 artists from different generations. The exhibition is on view in the galleries on the first floor of Istanbul Modern.

Renzo Piano: Genius Loci-Istanbul Modern.name: Renzo Piano: Genius Loci
Renzo Piano: Genius Loci-Istanbul Modern.description: “Renzo Piano: Genius Loci” focuses on the architecture of Istanbul Modern’s new museum building and its design and construction process, which spanned six years. Designed by Renzo Piano Building Workshop (RPBW), the new building greets art lovers at the same location where Istanbul Modern opened its doors in 2004 as Türkiye's first museum of modern and contemporary art.

Manuel \u00c7\u0131tak: An Island of One.name: Manuel Çıtak: An Island of One’s Own
Manuel \u00c7\u0131tak: An Island of One.description: The Istanbul Modern Photography Gallery hosts a solo exhibition of works by Manuel Çıtak (1962–2023), spanning from the 1980s, when he first took up photography, to his untimely passing in 2023. Comprising works that focus on human existence in the city, on urban peripheries, and across rural landscapes, “An Island of One’s Own” aims to illuminate Çıtak’s poetic dialogue with documentary photography.

Ali Kazma: Landscapes of the Mind-Istanb.name: Ali Kazma: Landscapes of the Mind
Ali Kazma: Landscapes of the Mind-Istanb.description: “Landscapes of the Mind” at Istanbul Modern Photography Gallery focuses on works revealing the writer’s mind through the metaphor of landscape painting by Ali Kazma (b. 1971), one of today’s leading lens-based artists, whose practice explores fundamental questions about the meaning of human activity. The exhibition features videos from the 2010s to the present focused on books and literature and a selection of photographs from the artist’s extensive archive.

\u00d6mer Ulu\u00e7: Beyond the Horizon-.name: Ömer Uluç: Beyond the Horizon
\u00d6mer Ulu\u00e7: Beyond the Horizon-.description: Istanbul Modern presents the solo exhibition of Ömer Uluç (1931–2010) titled “Beyond the Horizon,” which showcases his artistic journey. Bringing together different forms of expression that are key in the artist’s practice through various themes, it features a comprehensive selection of works from the 1960s to 2010.

\u0130zzet Keribar: Journey of Colors-Is.name: İzzet Keribar: Journey of Colors
\u0130zzet Keribar: Journey of Colors-Is.description: "Journey of Colors" presents a selection from İzzet Keribar's (b. 1936) vast archive of nearly 1.5 million images. The exhibition highlights the formal elements that have become the artist’s trademark, such as color, light, texture, and graphic composition. It also reveals the artist's evolving style over the years, inviting viewers on a vibrant journey through different times and places.

Chiharu Shiota: Between Worlds-Istanbul.name: Chiharu Shiota: Between Worlds
Chiharu Shiota: Between Worlds-Istanbul.description: Chiharu Shiota's solo exhibition “Between Worlds,” organized on Istanbul Modern’s invitation as part of the 100th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Japan and Türkiye, centers on the artist's sense of being “somewhere in between.” In shaping the exhibition’s conceptual framework, Shiota draws on Istanbul's location between Asia and Europe. She is also inspired by Istanbul Modern's location in Karaköy, one of the city’s busiest districts and home to its historic,…

Olafur Eliasson: Your unexpected encount.name: Olafur Eliasson: Your unexpected encounter
Olafur Eliasson: Your unexpected encount.description: Olafur Eliasson's first solo exhibition in Türkiye, “Your unexpected encounter,” reflects the artist's deep interest in light, color, perception, movement, geometry, and the environment. The artworks also reveal the network of relationships the artist forges between broad areas of research and his multidisciplinary practice. As well as following the personal journey of the artist, the exhibition addresses navigation and orientation on a wider scale, inspired by the site of the museum and its…

Ozan Sa\u011fd\u0131\u00e7: The Photogra.name: Ozan Sağdıç: The Photographer’s Testimony
Ozan Sa\u011fd\u0131\u00e7: The Photogra.description: “The Photographer’s Testimony” presents a wide selection of works by Ozan Sağdıç (b. 1934), one of the most prominent names in the history of photography in Türkiye. The exhibition focuses on documentary photography, a widespread genre of photography in the world, while also shedding light on the country’s social, political, economic, cultural, and visual history from the 1950s to the present day.

Flowing City-Istanbul Modern.name: Flowing City
Flowing City-Istanbul Modern.description: “Flowing City” explores the multilayered relationship between artistic production and water through the lens of Istanbul. From the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn to freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, and urban memory, the exhibition brings together contemporary artistic practices with classical paintings and historical photographs. Through local narratives and global perspectives, the selection invites visitors to reflect on water from past to present.

Yoko Ono: Insound and Instructure-Sak\u0.name: Yoko Ono: Insound and Instructure
Yoko Ono: Insound and Instructure-Sak\u0.description: Sabancı University Sakıp Sabancı Museum (SSM) presents the most comprehensive exhibition of Yoko Ono’s work ever presented in Türkiye, realised with the support of Akbank and in collaboration with MUSAC, Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Castilla y León in León, Spain. Yoko Ono: Insound and Instructure presents an extensive selection from over seventy years of artistic production by Yoko Ono, whose career began in the avant-garde milieu of New York in the late 1950s. Comprising 67 works, including…

Scribbled Exercises, Practice Pages-Sak\.name: Scribbled Exercises, Practice Pages
Scribbled Exercises, Practice Pages-Sak\.description: The exhibition “Scribbled Exercises, Practice Pages” brings together the scribbled exercises and practice pages of Ottoman calligraphers, presenting master calligraphers from the sixteenth to the twentieth century. The selection features scribbled exercises and practice pages from the Arts of the Book and Calligraphy Collection of Sabancı University Sakıp Sabancı Museum, alongside works from the collection of Kubbealtı Academy Cultural and Arts Foundation. It includes works by calligraphers…

Sak\u0131p Sabanc\u0131 Museum Painting.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum Painting Collection
Sak\u0131p Sabanc\u0131 Museum Painting.description: Approached through a thematic and chronological narrative that considers the forces shaping the changing visual culture of a given era, the Sakıp Sabancı Museum Painting Collection extends from nineteenth-century Ottoman painting to twentieth-century examples of modern Turkish art. Initiated by Sakıp Sabancı, a prominent businessperson, in the 1970s, and enriched over time through new acquisitions and long-term loans, the collection is presented to visitors in the museum’s modern galleries with…

Sak\u0131p Sabanc\u0131 Museum The Arts.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum The Arts of the Book and Calligraphy Collection
Sak\u0131p Sabanc\u0131 Museum The Arts.description: Sakıp Sabancı’s (d. 2004) collection of calligraphic works by famous calligraphers, Korans and illuminated manuscripts began with the purchase of a levha (calligraphic panel) by Sultan Mahmud II (r. 1808-39). From 1989 onwards it was exhibited in major museums abroad. The keen interest attracted by these exhibitions cemented Sakıp Sabancı and his family’s resolve to further enlarge the collection and encouraged the idea of founding a museum. In 1998 the family mansion Atlı Köşk (the Mansion…

Suzanne Lacy: Birlikte/Tog\u00e6ther-Sak.name: Suzanne Lacy: Birlikte/Togæther
Suzanne Lacy: Birlikte/Tog\u00e6ther-Sak.description: Sabancı University Sakıp Sabancı Museum presents Suzanne Lacy’s Birlikte/Togæther , the first exhibition in Turkey by the American artist and educator. Recognized as a pioneer of feminist art and of participatory, community-oriented performance, Lacy’s exhibition is on view through Sunday, March 8, 2026, with the support of the Sabancı Foundation. This first exhibition in Turkey presents selections from Suzanne Lacy’s long-term practice, which turns participation, solidarity, and mutual…

Georg Baselitz: The Last Decade-Sak\u013.name: Georg Baselitz: The Last Decade
Georg Baselitz: The Last Decade-Sak\u013.description: For tickets, click here . For the chronology text, click here . Georg Baselitz: The Last Decade at the Sabancı University Sakıp Sabancı Museum (SSM), with the support of Akbank, presents works by German painter, printmaker, and sculptor Georg Baselitz, a leading figure in contemporary art. The exhibition features close to one hundred large-scale paintings and sculptures created by Baselitz in the past decade, displayed throughout all gallery spaces and the garden of the SSM. Concurrently, a…

80 Years of Tomorrows-Salt Galata.name: 80 Years of Tomorrows
80 Years of Tomorrows-Salt Galata.description: Mastercard Exhibition Hall The exhibition 80 Years of Tomorrows traces the eighty-year history of Garanti BBVA through Turkey's economic, social…

Subsoil Onur G\u00f6kmen-Salt Galata.name: Subsoil Onur Gökmen
Subsoil Onur G\u00f6kmen-Salt Galata.description: Mastercard Exhibition Hall Onur Gökmen's exhibition Subsoil revisits a largely overlooked episode in the environmental and institutional history of…

Epipe G\u00fcne\u015f Terkol-Salt Galata.name: Epipe Güneş Terkol
Epipe G\u00fcne\u015f Terkol-Salt Galata.description: Mastercard Exhibition Hall Epipe is the culmination of an oral history and archival research project that Güneş Terkol has been working on with her…

Dark World-Salt Galata.name: Dark World
Dark World-Salt Galata.description: Mastercard Exhibition Hall Dark World investigates the intricate story of the film that shares its title, directed by Metin Erksan and written by Bedri…

Ali Tapt\u0131k, Merve Mepa, Asl\u0131 U.name: Ali Taptık, Merve Mepa, Aslı Uludağ
Ali Tapt\u0131k, Merve Mepa, Asl\u0131 U.description: Mastercard Exhibition Hall The projects selected for the first edition of the Salt Artistic Research and Production Grant Program, in collaboration with…

Ayamama Swa(m)p: Urban Resilience & Revi.name: Ayamama Swa(m)p: Urban Resilience & Revival of the River Corridor
Ayamama Swa(m)p: Urban Resilience & Revi.description: Workshop IV Salt is hosting an exhibition organized by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) School of Architecture and Planning. Centering on…

Translated into Socialism-Salt Galata.name: Translated into Socialism
Translated into Socialism-Salt Galata.description: Translated into Socialism presents the little-known history of the Turkish-speaking community in Yugoslavia, more precisely, in Kosovo and Macedonia. It…

Upcoming Exhibition: No Admittance Excep.name: Upcoming Exhibition: No Admittance Except on Business
Upcoming Exhibition: No Admittance Excep.description: Workplaces are among the most central yet least visible spaces of everyday life. These spaces, where the relationship between capital and labor is…

Across the Seas \u00d6zer Kaba\u015f and.name: Across the Seas Özer Kabaş and His Times
Across the Seas \u00d6zer Kaba\u015f and.description: Across the Seas: Özer Kabaş and His Times examines the practice of artist, educator, and writer Özer Kabaş (1934–1998)—ranging from painting and design to…

15 Years at Salt: Exhibition Posters-Sal.name: 15 Years at Salt: Exhibition Posters
15 Years at Salt: Exhibition Posters-Sal.description: Presented on the ground floor of Salt Beyoğlu, this installation brings together an extensive collection of posters produced for Salt’s exhibitions over…

Breaking Through a Dam-Salt Beyo\u011flu.name: Breaking Through a Dam
Breaking Through a Dam-Salt Beyo\u011flu.description: The word "landscape" has no exact equivalent in Arabic or Turkish; instead, different terms including arazi (land), manzara (view), or peyzaj (terrain)…

Trash-Salt Beyo\u011flu.name: Trash
Trash-Salt Beyo\u011flu.description: Are pedestals or display cases only meant to hold artworks? Does their life end when the exhibition closes, or can they assume different roles with each…

We've Been at the Tapestry Studio Since.name: We've Been at the Tapestry Studio Since the 90s
We've Been at the Tapestry Studio Since.description: The production of contemporary art and the discussions it sparked gained momentum in Turkey during the 1990s, establishing links with social and political…

Anatolian Plant Legacy-Salt Beyo\u011flu.name: Anatolian Plant Legacy
Anatolian Plant Legacy-Salt Beyo\u011flu.description: Kitchen Anatolian Plant Legacy brings together 80 works by 47 botanical artists, focusing on plants that have coexisted and interacted with humankind for…

The Lives of Animals-Salt Beyo\u011flu.name: The Lives of Animals
The Lives of Animals-Salt Beyo\u011flu.description: The Lives of Animals explores the evolving relationship between humans and animals throughout history—from coexistence to systems of domination. The…

Designer's Note-Salt Beyo\u011flu.name: Designer's Note
Designer's Note-Salt Beyo\u011flu.description: Designer's Note explores the rapid and profound evolution of graphic design in Türkiye during the late 20th century, focusing on a selection of books. The…

The Republic Behind the Scenes-Pera Muse.name: The Republic Behind the Scenes
The Republic Behind the Scenes-Pera Muse.description: Rooted in the Press Photography Archive of the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Photography Collection, The Republic Behind the Scenes focuses on the daily life of early republican Istanbul and the behind-the-scenes of photojournalism. Curated by İdil Çetin and Ahmet Ersoy, the exhibition makes visible the subjects that fall outside the era's ideological constructs and its polyphonic history through the unfiltered structure of the archive.

Frank Bowling: Creation and Destruction-.name: Frank Bowling: Creation and Destruction
Frank Bowling: Creation and Destruction-.description: With Interruptions by Francis Bacon and Victor Willing Frank Bowling: Creation and Destruction brings together works by Frank Bowling and two key figures from postwar British art, Francis Bacon and Victor Willing. With a spotlight on Frank Bowling, the exhibition traces the artistic paths of three painters as they converge, diverge and intersect once again.

Intersecting Worlds: Ambassadors and Pai.name: Intersecting Worlds: Ambassadors and Painters
Intersecting Worlds: Ambassadors and Pai.description: Ambassador Portraits and Art Patronage of Ambassadors from the 17th to the 19th Century Tracing the diplomatic contacts between the Ottoman Empire and Europe, the exhibition examines cross-cultural encounters through ambassadorial portraits and commissioned paintings. The ambassadors’ relationship with art reflects the political and social atmosphere of the period.

Osman Hamdi Bey-Pera Museum.name: Osman Hamdi Bey
Osman Hamdi Bey-Pera Museum.description: The life and art of Osman Hamdi Bey through his works in the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection An Ottoman intellectual raised by the TanzimatEra… An exceptional personality, who made substantial, diversified and lifelong contributions to various fields of culture and arts such as painting, archaeology, museology, and art education...

The Art of Weights and Measures-Pera Mus.name: The Art of Weights and Measures
The Art of Weights and Measures-Pera Mus.description: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Anatolian Weights and Measures Collection As the measurement of discovery became the substance of myths, weighing and measuring, beyond being mere physical actions, became an important means of self-expression to those captivated by the universe and what lay beyond the boundaries of knowledge.

Extraordinary Minas-Pera Museum.name: Extraordinary Minas
Extraordinary Minas-Pera Museum.description: The Story of Inspiration and Innovation in Kütahya Tiles and Ceramics The exhibition Extraordinary Minas , presenting objects from Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Kütahya Tiles and Ceramics Collection, examines the efforts of Kütahya masters in the late 19 th and early 20 th centuries to revive the disappearing craftsmanship of tile-making by focusing on a master and a group of his work. The exhibition explores the concepts of the master-apprentice relationship, tradition and innovation, and…

By the Water-Pera Museum.name: By the Water
By the Water-Pera Museum.description: The Life and Art of Halil Paşa By the Water: The Life and Art of Halil Paşa focuses on the life and artistic production of Halil Paşa, a key figure in the transformation of painting from the Ottoman Empire to the early Republican period. A military-trained painter, Halil Paşa brought together academic discipline and impressionist sensibility, playing a pioneering role in the emergence of the open-air painting tradition in Türkiye. The exhibition offers an in-depth exploration of the artist’s…

Feelings in Common-Pera Museum.name: Feelings in Common
Feelings in Common-Pera Museum.description: Works from the British Council Collection Feelings in Common is a contemporary group exhibition bringing together works of 29 artists from the British Council Collection. The exhibition, in striving to form a zone where feelings in common are shared amidst uncertainties and transformations regarding the future, approaches the British Council Collection from a contemporary and speculative viewpoint.

\u00c5sa Jungnelius-Pera Museum.name: Åsa Jungnelius
\u00c5sa Jungnelius-Pera Museum.description: A Verse, Written with Earth, Fire, Water, and Air Shaped through the interplay of glass—unsettling in its fragility—and stone—powerful in its permanence—this exhibition can be seen as a tribute to those who compose their own verse with the help of the four elements.

SAM\u0130H R\u0130FAT \"Much Is to Be Do.name: SAMİH RİFAT "Much Is to Be Done"
SAM\u0130H R\u0130FAT \"Much Is to Be Do.description: photographs, films, drawings, poems, notebooks, books, and music… "Much Is to Be Done" is an exhibition that departs from the both ethically and aesthetically uncompromising work of Samih Rifat, an important figure in the world of culture renowned for his photographs, translations, documentaries and writings. We could describe his work as “an act of art and thought”, and this exhibition aims to expand his creative process in order to understand this intellectual of “a thousand arts”, who sadly…

MARCEL DZAMA Dancing with the Moon-Pera.name: MARCEL DZAMA Dancing with the Moon
MARCEL DZAMA Dancing with the Moon-Pera.description: With a little help from his friend Raymond Pettibon Pera Museum is pleased to present Marcel Dzama’s first solo exhibition in Turkey, surveying the artist’s unique approach and compelling storytelling. The exhibition curated by Alistair Hicks, emerging from the artist’s colourful imaginative world that is centred on music and dance, is made up of works that address the failures of governance we are currently subjected to, environmental destruction, and the calamities caused by war.

Calculations and Coincidences-Pera Museu.name: Calculations and Coincidences
Calculations and Coincidences-Pera Museu.description: Dóra Maurer, Vera Molnár, Gizella Rákóczy Algorithmic Art from the Central Bank of Hungary Collection Calculations and Coincidences brought together three pioneers of algorithmic art—Vera Molnár, Dóra Maurer, and Gizella Rákóczy—through their works from the Hungarian National Bank Collection. The exhibition focused primarily on the profound influence of Molnár, who was unquestionably among the most significant names in computer art while tracing how the artistic explorations of Maurer and…

In Search of Vera Moln\u00e1r-Pera Museu.name: In Search of Vera Molnár
In Search of Vera Moln\u00e1r-Pera Museu.description: À La Recherche de Vera Molnár In Search of Vera Molnár (À La Recherche de Vera Molnár) offered a close look at the practice of Vera Molnár, one of the pioneers of computer art, and brought together works by contemporary artists inspired by her work.

There is no later. Later is here.-Arter.name: There is no later. Later is here.
There is no later. Later is here.-Arter.description: The world has already ended. World , not as in Planet Earth, but the constructed notion of the world : its politics, systems, social orders, and all constituent mechanisms that sustain them. “The end of the world” is not a future threat: it is a (ever-recycled) present condition. The systematic entrapments have become so entrenched that there is no alternative, no escape, no outside. Has a sudden catastrophic scenario – whether a meteor, a plague, or an alien invasion – become the only…

Mehtap Baydu: Loving You Is So Hard!-Art.name: Mehtap Baydu: Loving You Is So Hard!
Mehtap Baydu: Loving You Is So Hard!-Art.description: Mehtap Baydu’s first institutional solo exhibition in Türkiye, Loving You Is So Hard!, brings together new works conceived for this context alongside a selection of the artist’s recent pieces. The exhibition highlights the interconnections and transitions Baydu forges across diverse media such as performance, sculpture, photography and video, creating a layered sensory space where body and objects engage in a mutual interaction. At the heart of Loving You Is So Hard! lies a multiplicity that…

Tayfun Erdo\u011fmu\u015f: Atlas 1/137.0.name: Tayfun Erdoğmuş: Atlas 1/137.035999
Tayfun Erdo\u011fmu\u015f: Atlas 1/137.0.description: Plants, minerals, handmade papers, chemical and acrylic solutions constitute the material vocabulary of Tayfun Erdoğmuş. With diligence he gathers, accumulates, assorts, dissects, arranges, layers and preserves them. He invents original techniques and surfaces through lengthy processes rooted in experimentation. By facilitating the interactions, transformations and chance events through which matter takes on different states, he opens up a geography of his own, one that expands the established…

The Sky Was Candy-Arter.name: The Sky Was Candy
The Sky Was Candy-Arter.description: Conceived around the notions of “home” and “homeland”, the group exhibition The Sky Was Candy brings together works by 24 artists from the Arter Collection. Produced in a range of media including painting, photography, installation, sculpture and video, these works – some of which have joined the collection only recently – invite us to (re)connect with the houses entrusted with cherished memories or painful sorrows, the earth that layers our belongings, the homes we leave behind or carry within…

Work in Progress-Arter.name: Work in Progress
Work in Progress-Arter.description: Work In Progress exhibition is currently undergoing installation for its second stage; Galleries 0 and -1 are closed to visitors. In the exhibition’s second stage, opening on 24 November 2026, many of the works presented in the first chapter will give way to others, and new works realised within this context will also be incorporated into the exhibition. Work in Progress articulates a selection from over three hundred works produced with Arter’s support within the scope of its exhibitions…

Hera B\u00fcy\u00fckta\u015fc\u0131yan:.name: Hera Büyüktaşcıyan: Phantom Quartet
Hera B\u00fcy\u00fckta\u015fc\u0131yan:.description: Eugène Guillevic, Terraqué , 1942 “There is someone in the wind.” Phantom Quartet brings together Hera Büyüktaşcıyan’s newly produced works for this exhibition, along with a selection of earlier works, some drawn from the Arter Collection. The exhibition traverses the artist’s core engagement with the notions of invisibility, cyclicality, memory, architecture, the city and nature through her personal past rooted in the two neighbourhoods surrounding Arter – namely Kurtuluş and Tarlabaşı –, and…

Nilbar G\u00fcre\u015f: Velvet Stare-Art.name: Nilbar Güreş: Velvet Stare
Nilbar G\u00fcre\u015f: Velvet Stare-Art.description: Nilbar Güreş’s first institutional solo exhibition in Türkiye, Velvet Stare delves into the artist’s practice, which blurs the boundaries between humans and non-humans, reality and fiction, representation and abstraction. Presenting an extensive selection spanning from the artist’s early pieces to her most recent productions, the exhibition encompasses works realised in diverse media, including painting, engraving, collage, photography, sculpture, and video. Blending storytelling with critical…

Hah!-Arter.name: Hah!
Hah!-Arter.description: *An exclamation often used in a moment of sudden and unexpected revelation, or the laughter sparked by an incisively witty comment. Featuring video works selected from within and outside the Arter Collection, the group exhibition Hah! * explores satire’s role in criticising power mechanisms and reflecting on contemporary conditions. Oscillating between humour and gravity, the works highlight the struggles artists face in navigating institutional authority, gender normativity, and the…

I Need More Time-Arter.name: I Need More Time
I Need More Time-Arter.description: The production of the first photographs required not only light but also silence and long hours of time. Only two hundred years have passed, and cameras today are capable of shutter speeds as fast as 1/80,000 of a second. One wonders whether there exists any other device/thing that has so thoroughly reshaped its relationship with time in such a short period. Isn’t it something of an existential paradox that photography, always a few steps ahead in answering the world’s hunger for speed, strives…

Under Pressure Above Water-Arter.name: Under Pressure Above Water
Under Pressure Above Water-Arter.description: The group exhibition Under Pressure Above Water brings together 33 works by 15 artists across various media, including painting, sculpture, and photography, in Arter’s entrance and lower ground floor galleries. Structured around two interrelated sections, the exhibition explores the anxieties provoked by the uncertainties and social injustices of our time, such as environmental disasters, global conflicts, migration, and economic instability. Tracing the impact of challenging social conditions…

Franz Erhard Walther: Attempt to be a Sc.name: Franz Erhard Walther: Attempt to be a Sculpture
Franz Erhard Walther: Attempt to be a Sc.description: Year 1958. A young man is sitting before a sheet of canvas, cross-legged and barefoot, within close reach of a metal bowl containing a mixture of baking powder, water and milk. He spits out the mixture while a friend of his captures his ephemeral gestures with a camera. 19-year-old Franz Erhard Walther, growing up in Fulda (Germany), breaks from his family’s bakery business by expelling the ingredients involved in the making of bread. At the same time, with this action-work titled Attempt to be…

Kader Attia: Asesinos! Asesinos!-Arter.name: Kader Attia: Asesinos! Asesinos!
Kader Attia: Asesinos! Asesinos!-Arter.description: They are standing upright, in a tight arrangement. A hundred doors, split in half, each reassembled and positioned in an A-shape. Individuals of various heights, sizes and hues. Kader Attia’s large-scale installation Asesinos! Asesinos! situates us on a common ground where gravity rules. Grand narratives have long since collapsed. We have entered the era of the crowd. From now on, history is a terrain under permanent construction, composed of countless voices and individualities that weave past…

Koray Ari\u015f: The Skin We Live In-Art.name: Koray Ariş: The Skin We Live In
Koray Ari\u015f: The Skin We Live In-Art.description: The Skin We Live In brings together in a site-specific arrangement Koray Ariş’s works from different periods and series, as well as objects and materials documenting the production processes in his studio. The exhibition provides a comprehensive look into the artist’s six-decade-long sculptural practice through themes of figure, skin, sound, movement and balance that are pivotal in his oeuvre. The approximatively 300 works and objects on display embody a communal territory where the age-old…

Angelica Mesiti: Future Perfect Continuo.name: Angelica Mesiti: Future Perfect Continuous
Angelica Mesiti: Future Perfect Continuo.description: Angelica Mesiti’s solo exhibition Future Perfect Continuous borrows its title from the artist’s eponymous video in which eleven performers enact the sound of rain, as it varies over a wide spectrum. Starting softly as a gentle drizzle, the sound gradually intensifies, and, with a dramatic crescendo, transforms into a full-blown storm, before eventually receding and fading away, all conveyed through hand gestures and body percussion. The black-and-white video, inspired by a children’s game the…

Yasemin \u00d6zcan: Wet Floor-Arter.name: Yasemin Özcan: Wet Floor
Yasemin \u00d6zcan: Wet Floor-Arter.description: Yasemin Özcan’s solo exhibition Wet Floor explores the themes of intergenerational transmission, migration, and self-construction by delving into the complex relations between human beings and earth, language and remembrance, and autobiography and fiction. The exhibition brings together a selection of Özcan’s existing works with new pieces created especially for the gallery space at Arter. Soil permeates the exhibition, serving both as a basic construction material, and a metaphor for cultural…

Maaria Wirkkala: Landing Prohibited-Arte.name: Maaria Wirkkala: Landing Prohibited
Maaria Wirkkala: Landing Prohibited-Arte.description: Maaria Wirkkala’s Landing Prohibited, an installation which was displayed at the 52nd Venice Biennale in 2007 and acquired the same year by the Arter Collection, is now set to meet audiences in Istanbul for the first time. The artist, who spent her childhood not only in her homeland Finland’s Helsinki in the south, and Lapland in the north, but also Venice in Italy, has positioned the ever-shifting elements of these geographies, such as water, air and light, at the centre of her practice since…

Suppose You Are Not-Arter.name: Suppose You Are Not
Suppose You Are Not-Arter.description: Curated by Selen Ansen, the exhibition Suppose You Are Not probes the ways in which the domestic context of a private collection can be transferred into a museum context. In so doing, it explores the possibilities of restaging and articulating the affinities created between distinct objects by means of a collector's desires and endeavours. The exhibition, which spans the 4th and 3rd-floor galleries of Arter, brings together works by almost 400 artists, anonymous artefacts and mass-produced…

Jackie Matisse: Kite Time-Arter.name: Jackie Matisse: Kite Time
Jackie Matisse: Kite Time-Arter.description: Jackie Matisse (1931–2021) flew her signature kites in the skies over Istanbul almost half a century ago during a trip in 1976. It must not have even crossed the artist’s mind in those days that the Rainbow [Arc-en-Ciel, 1983] kites, which today appear in vivid colours inside the front windows of the Arter building, would invite passers-by to come in and explore the exhibition Kite Time .
